recentItems.title: Israel demolishes Palestinian prisoners’ homes in occupied West Bank
recentItems.description:
Israeli forces have demolished the homes of two Palestinian prisoners in the occupied West Bank, leaving their families homeless.
The men were detained last year over allegations that they were attempting to manufacture bombs and rockets.

Al Jazeera's Nida Ibrahim was there when the demolitions took place.

recentItems.title: At least 17 people killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa
recentItems.description:
At least 17 people have been killed in two separate shootings in South Africa.
Police say nine people were shot dead inside a shack in Jeffsville, an informal settlement near the capital, Pretoria.
Eight others were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle outside the city of Pietermaritzburg.

Al Jazeera’s Clement Manyathela reports from Pretoria, South Africa.

recentItems.title: Beyond the Horizon: Searching for Kenya's Elusive Black leopard
recentItems.description:
Maasai photographer Latei Moses is on a journey across northern Kenya to fulfil a lifelong ambition: to photograph the elusive black leopard, known locally as Giza. Believed to inhabit the remote region of Laikipia, the wild cat has long been the subject of local stories.

Latei's search takes him across difficult terrain, as he faces repeated setbacks and exhaustion. But his journey is about more than wildlife. The Maasai are among the most photographed communities in the world, often depicted through the eyes of outsiders. As a Maasai photographer, Latei is reclaiming the power of the camera, documenting his people on his terms. But can his persistence help him find Giza?

Beyond the Horizon: Searching for Giza is a documentary film by Mohtadi Ali Ahmad, Mohamad Ali Ahmad and Christelle Saade.

#documentary #aljazeeraenglish #Kenya #wildlife #photography

recentItems.title: Portugal Needs 400,000 Homes. But Who Will Build Them?
recentItems.description:
Portugal needs up to 400,000 new homes, but its construction industry says it is short of around 80,000 workers.

Migrant labour has been essential to the sector. Now tighter immigration rules are raising concerns about who will build the homes the country desperately needs.
